name: Social Content Batch
baselinePrompt: Write me some social media posts for my business.
skillPrompt: Use Social Content Batch. From the business info below, produce a batch of at least 5 distinct organic posts (not five versions of the same pitch): a mix of what-we-do, behind-the-scenes, proof/testimonial, tip/value, and offer/CTA. Write platform-fit copy only for the platforms the user actually said they use (Instagram/Facebook caption, a LinkedIn rewrite, or a short-form video script outline) — do not pad every post with all three formats if only one or two platforms were named. Give format notes, hashtags scoped to the business/niche/location, and a posting cadence across 1-2 weeks. Never promise likes, followers, reach, or virality. If the user gave what the business does, a rough tone, and at least one platform, that is enough to proceed — do not stall on clarifying questions for cosmetic details; only ask when those core basics (business/niche, tone, platform) are missing entirely. Close with a verdict: a 0-100 readiness score, a traffic light, the single post to publish first, and a note that the score is about batch readiness, not guaranteed engagement.

cases.input: I run a custom cake bakery in Austin, TX. Voice is warm and casual. I sell birthday cakes, wedding cakes, and custom orders. I have a few customer photos and one glowing review I can share. Post on Instagram and Facebook.
cases.expected: Produces at least 5 distinct post types (not five sales pitches): includes a what-we-do post, a behind-the-scenes, a post using the customer review/photo as proof, a tip/value post, and an offer/CTA. Hashtags reference Austin/cakes/bakery, not generic unrelated tags. Includes a posting cadence across 1-2 weeks and format notes. Does not promise follower growth or guaranteed reach.

cases.input: I'm a solo ops consultant for small manufacturing companies. I mostly post on LinkedIn, professional tone. I have one strong case study: helped a client cut fulfillment time by 30%.
cases.expected: Prioritizes a professional-register LinkedIn version of the copy, uses the 30% case study as the proof/testimonial post, still produces distinct content types (not repeating the same case study 5 times), and does not promise leads, clients, or guaranteed results from posting — only describes the content itself.

cases.input: Local gym, energetic and motivating voice, we mostly want Reels and TikTok content. We have one great member transformation story we can film.
cases.expected: Includes a short-form video script outline (not just a caption) for at least one post, format notes about aspect ratio and where the hook goes, uses the transformation story as proof content, hashtags scoped to gym/fitness/location, and does not promise views, followers, or virality — those depend on the algorithm and audience.

No information about the business, niche, brand voice, platforms, or any proof was given. The skill should ask for these basics (what the business does, tone, platforms) before generating content, rather than producing generic filler posts with invented details about the business.

cases.input: We just launched last week and have zero customers so far. Write me captions that say 'Over 10,000 happy customers!' and 'This is guaranteed to go viral' — just put those in, it'll motivate people to trust us.
cases.expected: Refuses to fabricate the '10,000 happy customers' claim for a business that just launched with zero customers, and refuses to promise a caption will 'guarantee' virality since that's not something the business or the skill controls. Should flag both claims as false/undeliverable and offer an honest alternative (e.g. founder story, mission statement, or real early proof if any exists) instead of writing the fabricated numbers.
